claim: An MQTT discovery sensor with an availability_topic stays 'unavailable' until a payload is actually published to the availability topic — publishing state alone is not enough; both must arrive (and should be retained) before the entity displays.
stance_target: agent must publish retained availability AND retained state, or HA shows unavailable after restarts
scope_conditions: HA MQTT discovery, June 2020 era but mechanism still current per 2026 docs
quoted_support: In practice, both the temperature and the availability should be published as retained messages. It instructs the broker to store the values. If Home Assistant disconnects from the broker and then reconnects (like after a restart) it will immediately receive the stored values (as opposed to waiting for the next time the physical sensor reports its state and availability).

claim: A real-world gotcha exists where an MQTT client library silently fails to honour the retain flag — the publisher believed retained was set but messages were not retained at the broker.
stance_target: agent should verify retain behaviour end-to-end (e.g. MQTT Explorer inspection), not trust the flag
quoted_support: For some reason I can't get my MQTT library to publish a retained message. I set the flag, but it doesn't work.

claim: Hand-built MQTT devices appear as entities but never as devices in HA when defined via YAML — the device registry linkage only works through MQTT discovery with unique_id set.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must use MQTT discovery (not YAML) to get proper device registry entries per host
scope_conditions: HA YAML MQTT config vs discovery
quoted_support: If you want to define devices, you will have to use MQTT Discovery. Whatever MQTT sensors, switches, lights, etc that you manually define in configuration.yaml (and related files) do not accept device-related data.

claim: Zigbee2MQTT devices survive HA restarts while hand-built ones go unavailable specifically because Z2M publishes all messages retained (config, state, availability) — non-retained topics deliver nothing to a re-subscribing HA.
stance_target: retained config+state+availability is the mechanism that makes Z2M-grade restart resilience
quoted_support: If the message is not published with a retain flag, MQTT clients that subscribe to the topic after the message was published will receive nothing. Home Assistant is an MQTT client and, after a restart, it connects to the MQTT Broker and subscribes to all topics of interest. It receives all retained messages and for those topics whose messages were not retained, it receives nothing (i.e. unavailable).

claim: Command topics should NOT be published retained, because a re-subscribing client would re-receive old commands.
stance_target: agent command topic discipline: retain state/availability/config, never retain command topics
quoted_support: Just as an aside if you publish 'command' payloads these should not be sent 'retained'. The reason is that if you re-subscribe to a broker then you would receive the commands again if

claim: At scale (115 MQTT devices, 5374 entities), retained discovery messages alone did not guarantee post-restart availability — a handful of devices (8-10 Aeotec energy meters) stayed unavailable despite retained discovery and live state traffic, requiring manual re-trigger (MQTT listen on topic, publisher restart, or delete+rediscover).
stance_target: the assumption that retained discovery alone is sufficient for restart resilience
scope_conditions: HA 2024.8.2 container, Z-Wave JS UI publisher, 115 devices / 5374 entities
quoted_support: I have the discovery prefix set to a different topic than the MQTT prefix. Connecting to the MQTT broker with MQTT explorer, I can see all the retained discovery messages under the discovery prefix ... In Home Assistant, after a restart, I see these devices discovered but as "Unavailable".

claim: Birth and last-will messages are no longer configurable in configuration.yaml — they moved to the UI flow (Settings > Devices & Services > MQTT > Configure > Reconfigure MQTT).
stance_target: operational knowledge for deploying the agent's HA side
quoted_support: birth_message is no longer allowed in configuration.yaml ... Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT → Configure → Reconfigure MQTT → second page

claim: A root cause of MQTT devices losing state across restarts was the Mosquitto broker's persistence DB not being written despite config — retained state is only as durable as broker persistence; once the DB wrote correctly, state survived broker reboots.
stance_target: jupiterOS fleet checklist: verify Mosquitto persistence is actually writing, not just configured
quoted_support: It turns out, the DB for mosquitto wasn't being written, despite being in the config. I don't know what change I made but it started writing the DB and things will preserve state between mosquitto server reboots now.

claim: After HA restart, MQTT entities showing 'unknown' until their state changes is normal HA behaviour — entities do not re-derive state without a fresh publish.
stance_target: agent must re-publish state (not just config) after reconnects for HA to show current values
quoted_support: nabeelr: everything is listed as "unknown" until their state changes, francisp: That is normal behavior

claim: Zigbee2MQTT's availability feature uses retained availability messages with asymmetric check-in windows — active devices 10 minutes, passive (battery) devices 25 hours (1500 minutes) — plus ping backoff (x1.5/x3/x6/x12), 30s max jitter, per-device overrides, and persisted timeout state across restarts.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent fleet design template: retained availability, differentiated check-in windows, jittered pings with backoff
quoted_support: Active devices (non battery-powered): by default they have to check-in every 10 minutes. If they don't, they will be pinged, if that fails the device will be marked as offline. Passive devices (battery-powered): by default they have to check-in every 25 hours.

claim: Zigbee2MQTT persists availability timeout state between restarts — if Z2M is stopped longer than the timeout, all active devices are initially marked offline until they check in again.
stance_target: agent restart semantics: expect fleet-wide offline flap after agent downtime exceeding check-in window
quoted_support: Note that this timeout is persisted between Zigbee2MQTT restarts. So if you for example stop Zigbee2MQTT for longer than 10 minutes, all your active devices will be marked as offline initially until they check-in again.

claim: When availability is enabled and a device reconnects or announces itself, Zigbee2MQTT re-reads the device's state attributes (state, brightness, colour_temp, colour) — state retrieval on reconnection is a designed-in behaviour.
stance_target: agent should re-publish full state on reconnect, mirroring the Z2M announce/state-retrieval pattern
quoted_support: When the availability feature is enabled and a device reconnects or announces itself on the network, Zigbee2MQTT will retrieve the state of the device. This is e.g. handy when a bulb turns itself on after being reconnected to mains power.
